title: Sanjō Ōhashi Bridge
visualBrief: Present steel nine-span bridge with the completed2024 hinoki railings, fourteen retained bronze giboshi, timber girder covers, circular stone shoes and multi-column frames, renewed silver-gray checker paving and modeled asanoha-pattern pedestrian barriers.

sourceFacts.structuralType: Simply supported steel I-girder spans on multi-column rigid-frame piers and direct foundations
sourceFacts.ownerSource: Kyoto City Construction Bureau, October2024 Roads Administration Seminar report

reconstruction.notes: Published structure dimensions and main-post counts govern this model. Span spacing, girder and pier sections, rail spacing, road layout, detailed bronze profile and foundation depth are reconstructed from owner photographs. Fine historical inscriptions are not yet sculpted.

geographicProposal.notes: Exact retained bridge anchor and signed axis; authored73.3x16.7m dimensions. Shared-material browser levels retain source proportions with corrected30cm curbs and green post clamps. Standard PMTiles/Mapzen supplies native water/terrain/approach geometry; bounded bridge/approach ground openings avoid coarse bank burial. Original detailed source master is byte-preserved.

groundCutout.basis: Only the bridge and immediate straight approach ribbons reconstruct a bounded rendered bank. Terrain above sourceY0.45m is capped there; lower terrain, original DEM samples, native water, paving and buildings remain unchanged. This prevents coarse high banks from covering the bridge or leaving sky holes underneath. The rendered cap is approximate, not surveyed riverbed. The inset bridge interior also caps intersecting native river-walk paving at the same bank level, preserving its original route; approach joins outsideX±36.6m retain their authored deck elevations.

geographicProposal.groundContactBasis: Provisional standard-viewer water fit: native Kamo water at the bridge center is42.150093m; source footing bases are placed at41.70m, approximately0.45m submerged. The former west-bank DSM reference placed bases2.33m above water and is rejected. This is a local visualization datum, not a surveyed elevation or dynamic river stage.

geometrySource: Original deterministic exterior geometry. No downloaded meshes or embedded photographs.
sourceLicense: Repository license for original geometry; map-derived plan © OpenStreetMap contributors ODbL-1.0; reference publications retain their own rights.
materialMethod: Canonical shared material graphs with metric UV repeats and per-component vertex tints; separate transparent glazing; no model-specific bitmap textures.
reviewStatus: source-geometry; current renders and geographic fit require review

identityFeatures: Nine-span steel deck and eight multi-column pier frames
Pale hinoki railings with fourteen retained patinated bronze giboshi
Fine checker sidewalks and open asanoha-pattern roadway barriers
appearance.sourceMaster: Detailed geometry retained; browser derivatives replace subpixel repeat geometry with reusable analytic shared surfaces.
appearance.identity: Nine cambered spans on repeated multi-column frames, pale hinoki rails and fourteen green bronze giboshi, open hemp-leaf barriers and fine gray checker walks.
appearance.exclusions: Statues, traffic, interiors, surveyed foundations, historic inscriptions/sword scars and dynamic lighting control.

limitations: Fine historic finial inscriptions and individual sword scars require additional close photographic evidence.
Adjacent statues, street signs, temporary furniture and vegetation are outside this bridge asset.

The original detailed master retains its earlier18cm curb/dark-clamp interpretation. Current browser levels correct the visible curb to30cm and near post clamps to patinated bronze; the original detailed source recipe/bytes remain preserved.

Ordinary photographs and standard PMTiles/Mapzen guide this current review. The retained GSI study is historical evidence and is not fetched or required for normal builds or the current placement fixture.

Near river stage and bank/road widths remain generalized; source pier proportions and seven-column schedule are retained without a new fabrication survey. Physical laptop/phone timings remain pending.

Footing placement uses a provisional local water fit, not surveyed foundation levels. Coarse terrain beside the bounded bridge/approach openings can remain steep, and distant road grades are generalized. No native water or terrain samples are changed.

A bounded native-terrain cap at sourceY0.45m reconstructs dry banks beneath the bridge/immediate approaches where coarse DSM is too high. Native heightfield samples and water remain exact; the cap and steep outer bank transitions are visualization approximations.

Intersecting native river-walk paving receives a bounded underpass grade at the same bank cap inside the inset bridge footprint. Its original route remains; exact ramps and historical riverside steps are not reconstructed.
importReason: Preserve thin cables, rail frames and hardware across the full crossing; whole-object quantization loses these details.
